commands.author: coygeek

target.title: [security] External provider skips SSH credential destination validation
target.body:
# [security] External provider skips SSH credential destination validation

## Summary

The External provider can build an SSH lease target from repository-sourced `external.connection.ssh` configuration, including the destination host and key path. Crabbox already treats repository-selected SSH/control destinations as sensitive when they can inherit a key, SSH agent, or local SSH configuration from a more trusted source, but the credential-destination provenance checker has no External-provider case.

This crosses the supported Crabbox boundary for a lower-trust configuration source selecting where trusted credentials are used. A malicious or compromised repository can configure `provider: external`, point `external.connection.ssh.host` at an attacker-controlled SSH server, and either omit `external.connection.ssh.key` so ambient SSH configuration/agent authentication is used or set it to an absolute/operator-local key path. The SSH private key is not normally transmitted by SSH public-key authentication, so the issue is credential-destination misuse rather than raw private-key file exfiltration; the missing guard still lets repository config silently route trusted SSH authentication material and local SSH configuration effects to an unapproved host.

## Affected Components

- `internal/cli/credential_provenance.go:20-77`: The credential provenance structure tracks many provider destination and credential fields, including Static SSH, Parallels, and exe.dev fields, but has no External SSH host or key provenance fields.
- `internal/cli/credential_provenance.go:220-351`: `validateProviderCredentialDestination` rejects repository-selected credential destinations for many providers and includes Static SSH, Parallels, and exe.dev cases, but has no `external` case.
- `internal/cli/credential_provenance.go:389-395`: The existing SSH destination helper treats an empty key as ambient SSH configuration/agent authentication and treats repository-escaping keys as inherited credentials, which is exactly the protection missing for the External provider.
- `internal/cli/config.go:473-493`: `ExternalConnectionConfig` includes `SSH.Host`, `SSH.Key`, `ProxyCommand`, and related SSH routing/authentication fields.
- `internal/cli/config.go:3565-3574`: Repository YAML can define the External provider `connection` block through `fileExternalConfig.Connection`.
- `internal/cli/config.go:5716-5741`: File-loaded External configuration copies `file.External.Connection` into `cfg.External.Connection` without the trusted-source guards used for some other sensitive provider settings.
- `internal/providers/external/lifecycle.go:402-445`: Declarative External lifecycle mode builds the lease response from `cfg.External.Connection`, including the configured SSH block.
- `internal/providers/external/lifecycle.go:448-499`: `lifecycleSSH` expands `external.connection.ssh.host` and `external.connection.ssh.key` into a protocol SSH target.
- `internal/providers/external/protocol.go:127-168`: The protocol lease target copies the expanded SSH `Host` and `Key` into the `SSHTarget` that Crabbox will use.
- `internal/providers/external/backend.go:92-121`: External acquisition converts the protocol response into a lease and then calls `WaitForSSHReady` against that SSH target.
- `internal/cli/ssh.go:601-645`: Crabbox invokes OpenSSH with the target host and, when a key is set, passes `-i <key>` and `IdentitiesOnly=yes`; when no key is set, ambient SSH configuration and agent behavior can still apply.
- `SECURITY.md:34-49`: The maintainer policy lists "Crabbox silently sending a trusted credential to a destination selected by a different, lower-trust configuration source" as an in-scope boundary.
- `docs/security.md:257-271`: The operational guide says repository-selected Static SSH, Parallels, and exe.dev control hosts cannot inherit keys, SSH agents, or local SSH configuration from a more trusted source without same-source credentials or an explicit destination approval; External is not covered by that documented guard.

## Attack Path

An attacker controls a repository or a repository-local `.crabbox.yaml` that a trusted operator reviews insufficiently and then uses with Crabbox. The repository config selects the External provider and supplies a declarative connection such as an attacker-controlled SSH host plus either an omitted SSH key, which falls back to ambient SSH configuration/agent behavior, or an operator-local absolute key path.

When the operator runs a Crabbox command that acquires or resolves the External lease, `applyFileConfigWithTrust` copies the repository External connection into `cfg.External.Connection`. The generic provider credential-destination validator runs before provider setup, but it has no External-provider case, so it does not reject the repository-selected SSH destination combined with inherited SSH authentication. External lifecycle code then expands the configured SSH fields, returns them as a protocol lease, converts that protocol lease into an `SSHTarget`, and waits for SSH readiness against the attacker-selected host.

The resulting SSH client invocation uses the repository-selected host and either the configured inherited key path or the operator's ambient SSH configuration/agent. That is the same lower-trust-destination pattern the project already blocks for Static SSH, Parallels, and exe.dev, but it is currently missing for External.

## Impact

A repository can silently choose where Crabbox uses trusted SSH authentication material and local SSH configuration effects for the External provider. At minimum, an attacker-controlled SSH server can receive an attempted authentication from the operator's configured SSH identity and learn identity/proof-of-possession information that the operator did not explicitly approve for that destination. In deployments where the operator's ambient SSH configuration enables stronger behaviors such as agent use, host-specific options, proxy commands, or agent forwarding, the blast radius can include stronger credential-use side effects.

This is not a hostile multi-tenant isolation claim and does not depend on arbitrary tenants sharing a broker. The supported boundary is the maintainer-documented credential-destination boundary: a lower-trust repository source should not be able to silently redirect inherited trusted credentials to its chosen destination.

## Severity Assessment

### CVSS Assessment

| Metric | v3.1 | v4.0 |
|--------|------|------|
| **Score** | 7.4 / 10.0 | 6.9 / 10.0 |
| **Severity** | High | Medium |
| **Vector** | `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` | `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` |
| **Calculator** | [CVSS v3.1 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) | [CVSS v4.0 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4.0#CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) |

The score reflects network-reachable attacker infrastructure, low attack complexity, no Crabbox privileges for the repository author, and required operator interaction to run Crabbox on the repository. The rating is driven by credential-destination misuse and trusted SSH authentication exposure; it intentionally does not claim direct private-key file disclosure or a proven direct impact on a separate subsequent system.

## Recommended Remediation Approach

Extend the credential provenance model to track External SSH host, key, proxy, and related authentication-destination fields. Add External-provider validation equivalent to the existing Static SSH and Parallels protections: repository-selected External SSH destinations should be allowed only when the credential material is same-source and contained by the repository, or when the operator explicitly approves the destination through a trusted flag, environment variable, user config, or another reviewed control.

Treat empty External SSH keys as inherited ambient authentication, and treat absolute, missing, or repository-escaping key paths as inherited credentials unless an explicit trusted override approves the destination. Consider disabling or overriding dangerous ambient SSH options for External-provider connections unless they are explicitly operator-approved. Update the operational security guide so External is listed with the other repository-selected SSH/control destinations, and add regression tests covering repository-sourced External SSH hosts combined with ambient authentication, absolute key paths, repository-contained keys, and explicit trusted overrides.

## Validation

I verified this against the latest target snapshot at commit `5b39acb1d8d0530824f1acc25d73b94bc9a0c773`.

Positive evidence:

- The maintainer security policy makes this boundary in scope: lower-trust configuration must not silently select where trusted credentials are sent or used.
- The operations guide already applies this exact protection pattern to repository-selected Static SSH, Parallels, and exe.dev destinations.
- External configuration exposes SSH host/key/proxy fields to repository YAML and copies the connection block without trusted-source filtering.
- The generic credential-destination validator has no External-provider branch, so the existing SSH-destination helper is never applied to External.
- External lifecycle mode expands configured SSH host/key fields into a protocol lease and Crabbox then attempts SSH readiness against that target.

Counterevidence and limits:

- SSH public-key authentication normally proves possession locally and does not transmit the private key bytes to the server; the report should be treated as credential-destination misuse, not direct private-key file exfiltration.
- External lifecycle has separate protections against environment-derived `resourceName` values by default, but those controls do not validate the SSH credential destination.
- Repository configuration is generally executable project automation in Crabbox's trust model; this report remains in scope because the maintainer policy separately calls out lower-trust configuration selecting trusted credential destinations as a supported boundary.
